Alex — thanks again for your time today. Quick written recap + proposed handoff items so we’re aligned heading into the POC:

- Embed patient-relevant text for semantic search + a reranking pass for top-k results.
- Local sandbox run: run Python and TypeScript sample apps against a local dockerized model proxy and validate auth & routing.

- Sample apps (two small repos: structured-output-toolcall example + embeddings->reranker flow).
- A one-page auth note: options (API key for sandbox vs OAuth/SSO for production) + KMS pointers.
- A diagram of the embeddings pipeline and where reranker slots in.

3) Asks from Lumina before POC start
- Confirm which internal team will run the sandbox (eng vs ops) and an email for the account used to request trial capacity.
- A short sample dataset (CSV of ~500 de-identified notes) and an example prompt/label set to validate structured extraction.

4) Logistics / timeline
- Proposed start: next Monday (2028-09-30).
- Redwood will send quickstart + sample-apps by EOD tomorrow (2028-09-25).
- Weekly 30-min sync during POC (Wednesdays).

Attachments sent: redwood_local_quickstart.md, sample-apps.zip (small repos).

Alex — quick technical notes and two short code snippets to get your eng-ops team started. See inline + attachments (embedding pipeline diagram).

Auth & sandbox
- For POC: REDWOOD_API_KEY (scoped key with expiry) in env is simplest. We’ll surface token rotation steps in the quickstart.
- For production: we support OIDC with SCIM for SSO + KMS integration (we’ll send the production checklist separately).

Routing & model selection
- Use the "X-Redwood-Route" header to pin requests to "low-latency" or "high-accuracy" lanes. The SDKs also accept a route param.

Structured output (tool-calling) snippet — TypeScript (pseudo):

// structured-toolcall.ts (excerpt)
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference-js';
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const resp = await client.call({
  model: 'redwood-rc-structured-v1',
  input: 'Extract diagnosis codes from the note and return JSON schema',
  structured_output: { schema: { type: 'object', properties: { codes: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, confidence: { type: 'number' } } } },
  route: 'high-accuracy'
});

// resp.output will be JSON-parsed according to the schema above

Embeddings + reranker flow (Python pseudo):

# embeddings_rerank.py (excerpt)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])

# 1) get embeddings for query and docs
q_emb = client.embeddings.create(input=query_text)
doc_embs = client.embeddings.create(input=doc_texts)

# 2) local vector search (FAISS) -> candidate ids
candidates = local_faiss.search(q_emb, top_k=50)

# 3) reranker: score top candidates with a light model call
rank_scores = client.rerank(score_model='redwood-rerank-mini', query=query_text, candidates=top_docs)
# sort by score and return top-k

Notes: for POC you can run FAISS locally; once you move to dedicated infra we recommend Milvus/ManagedVectorDB for scale.

Attachments: embeddings_pipeline_diagram.png (simple flow diagram).

If useful I can drop a small docker-compose that runs a local faiss service + the proxy for the SDK calls — I’ll include that in the sample-apps.zip.

—Rishi
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
